title: Household Add-On Membership: when a removal may be recorded
content:
## Product and scope
This document states the Household Add-On Membership basis for which add-on statuses a removal, whether requested by the primary member or carried out administratively after nonpayment, may be recorded against.

## Rule
A removal may be recorded against a household add-on only while that add-on's record shows a status of active or suspended.

## Eligibility: what must be true before a removal may be recorded
- Applicable event: a removal being recorded against a household add-on, whether the primary member's own voluntary removal or an administrative removal after nonpayment.
- Authority: the add-on's status is read from the system's own record of that add-on, not from anything the customer states on the call.
- Object correlation: the status checked is the status of the specific add-on record the removal is being recorded against.
- Allowed statuses: active or suspended.

## Points of judgement
- Because only active or suspended is allowed, a removal may not be recorded against an add-on whose record shows applied (not yet activated) or closed; those two statuses fall outside the allowed range.
- The same allowed-status basis governs both a voluntary removal at the primary member's request and an administrative removal carried out after nonpayment; the rule does not distinguish between the two by status.

## Boundary case (illustrative only)
An add-on whose record shows suspended may have a removal recorded against it, because suspended is within the allowed range. An add-on whose record already shows closed may not have a further removal recorded against it, because closed falls outside the allowed range.
